$comment: SERVICES MANIFEST — copy this to services.json and edit it for your machine.
The manager starts this file MISSING by copying it, so on a fresh clone you
get a working (if useless) configuration rather than a crash. Then you edit
it. Every path below is a placeholder.
A SERVICE is a program on this machine that an MCP server depends on — a
browser to drive, a local model server, a 3D application. The manager probes
it, starts it when a request needs it, and stops it.
Fields:
id        short unique identifier, no spaces (it becomes an argument to the MCP tools)
label     human-readable name, shown in the UI and the tray
why       WHY this service exists. This is what an agent reads first.
notes     list of traps / preconditions / ordering (the KNOWLEDGE)
requires  ids of other services that must be running BEFORE this one
start     { exe, args }  or  { cmd, args }   -> how to launch it
stop      { process }     or  { cmd, args }   -> how to stop it
probe     { process } or { http, expect } or { port }   -> how to tell whether it runs
Probe 'http':    GET the URL; alive if the status is in 'expect' (default 2xx).
Probe 'process': a process with that name exists.
Probe 'port':    something is listening on that local TCP port.
start.exE is launched detached, so it survives the manager. Leave 'args' out
if the program needs none.
stop.only_if_cmdline_matches is the important one: it kills only the processes
whose command line contains that string. That is what lets you stop 'the debug
Chrome' without closing the browser you are actually using.

services.label: Chrome (debug port)
services.why: A browser an agent can drive, over the Chrome DevTools Protocol.
notes: A dedicated --user-data-dir is MANDATORY: since Chrome 136, remote debugging is refused on the default profile.
This is a SECOND browser with its own profile, so it has none of your cookies or logins.
The playwright MCP server ATTACHES to this Chrome; it never launches one itself.

services.label: Local model server (example: an HTTP probe)
services.why: Placeholder for a local inference server your MCP servers talk to.
notes: The first call after an idle period is slow: the model has to load.
If your server exposes a health endpoint, probe THAT rather than the API root.

services.label: Desktop application (example: a process probe)
services.why: Placeholder for an application that only exposes its tools while it is open.
notes: Some applications load their MCP adapter INSIDE themselves, at startup. There is no separate server to launch — the application being open IS the server.
That is why the probe is by process: there is no port to test.
Starting it opens a window. That is not a quiet background start, and it is worth saying so in the notes.
